newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares heady climb seen overdone.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares heady climb seen overdone.

text.p: Strong gains in Belgian shares on Wednesday amid relief over U.S. interest rate policy could be overdone, dealers said.
"Maybe we have room to go a bit higher...but in November once the U.S. elections are out of the way I think we will see a correction," said an analyst at brokerage Mignon Hanart Declerck.

Traders said Wednesday's rise, which took the Bel-20 index to 1,764.43, 13.97 points over Tuesday's close, was due to the wave of relief that swept European markets after the U.S. Federal Reserve left its interest rates unchanged on Tuesday.
Most of Belgium's gains came in busy afternoon trade when purchases of baskets of the shares making up the index boosted volume.
All the Bel-20 heavyweights benefited from the move, one dealer said. Bekaert rose 475 to 23,800 francs. Kredietbank rose 200 to 10,350 francs. UCB gained 600 to 60,600.
He added, however, that with volume of around three billion francs it was a well supported, general move rather than an attempt by speculators to push up the index.

One of the less liquid stocks to post gains in heavier than normal volume was shipping company CMB, which ended up 45 at 2,495 francs. Dealers said players were accumulating the stock purely because of the prospect of a 200 franc interim dividend next week.
"That's a gross yield of about eight percent which is not bad when you look at where interest rates are," one trader said. "But it's the only reason to buy."
